titleText.es: ¡No os preocupéis! Desde el punto de vista de la luz, su casa y vuestro ojo son el mismo lugar, ¡y el viaje no dura nada en absoluto! La relatividad nos vuelve a alegrar el día.
titleText.en: Don't worry! From the light's point of view, home and your eye are in the same place, and the journey takes no time at all! Relativity saves the day again.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish and English texts are the exact title attributes from the Spanish archive and official xkcd. The wording playfully assigns light a point of view; strictly, light has no valid inertial rest frame.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Estrellas is the plural of estrella. It can name astronomical stars or star-shaped figures.
Llega is a present form of llegar for one person or thing. Llegar takes a before the destination or endpoint.

example.es: El tren llega a la estación a las ocho.
example.en: The train reaches the station at eight.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: we can; we may (special form after a purpose or uncertainty)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Podamos is a present subjunctive form of poder for nosotros. A purpose introduced by para que calls for this special form because its result is intended rather than stated as a fact.

example.es: Habla despacio para que podamos entender.
example.en: Speak slowly so that we can understand.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Puntos can mean small visible dots, mathematical points, score points, or periods in writing. Use the surrounding noun or description to choose the intended sense.

example.es: Hay tres puntos negros en la pantalla.
example.en: There are three black dots on the screen.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Bonitos ends in -os to describe a masculine plural noun. The other forms are bonito, bonita, and bonitas.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone or something reaches a destination?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching form of llegar, then a, then name the destination.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Llegar changes for the person and time, while a remains before the endpoint. A plus el contracts to al; a plus la, los, or las stays separate.

example.es: La carta llegó a su destino.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: tan lejos de + lugar o referencia
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something is so far from a place or reference point?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use tan lejos de followed by the place or reference point.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Tan intensifies lejos, and de introduces the reference point. Change tan to muy for the ordinary statement ‘very far from.’

example.es: Nunca había estado tan lejos de casa.
example.en: I had never been so far from home.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: luz de las estrellas · viaje · relatividad
cardDefinitions.questionEn: What scientific ideas make the starlight's journey both poignant and funny?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Ancient photons cross enormous distances before an eye absorbs them, while the title jokes that relativity makes the trip instantaneous for the light itself.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Seeing occurs when light reaches and is absorbed by the eye, so the dialogue personifies that detection as the light arriving only to die. The title invokes the zero proper time along a lightlike path, but saying ‘from light's point of view’ is deliberately informal: a photon has no valid inertial rest frame.

applications.explanationEn: Para introduces the poetic purpose, and morir stays in its unchanged -ir form.
Tan intensifies the distance word lejos, and de introduces casa as the reference point.
Para que introduces the intended result, and podamos is the special non-factual form used because that result is a purpose.
Podamos supplies the changed form of poder, while ver stays in its unchanged -er form.
Bonitos follows puntos and describes their appearance.
Bonitos uses masculine plural -os to agree with puntos.
